subject: Communication
title: Microexpressions: Emotions in a Flash
description: One-minute skill: Microexpressions: Emotions in a Flash.

hook.text: A genuine emotion flashes across someone's face for 1/25th of a second. You missed it. But it was there.

buildup.text: Microexpressions are involuntary facial expressions that occur too fast to consciously suppress.

discovery.text: Ekman discovered them by slow-motion analysis of therapy patients who claimed to be happy but weren't.

twist.text: Most people can't spot microexpressions naturally. But training improves detection rates significantly.

climax.text: Security agencies and therapists train in microexpression reading to detect concealed emotions.

punchline.text: The truth shows on your face. You just can't hide it fast enough.

quiz.question: How long does a microexpression typically last?

details.summary: Microexpressions are involuntary facial expressions lasting less than half a second. They reveal concealed emotions before the person can mask them, making them valuable for reading genuine feelings.
details.whyItMatters: Spotting microexpressions can help detect hidden emotions in negotiations, interviews, and relationships, though training and accuracy vary widely.
takeaways: Microexpressions last one-fifth to one-half of a second
They are involuntary and difficult to suppress consciously
Training improves detection but does not make it foolproof

faq.question: Can anyone learn to spot microexpressions reliably?
faq.answer: Research shows training improves detection rates from chance levels to roughly 70-80%. However, real-world accuracy is lower because context, baseline behavior, and individual variation all complicate interpretation.

faq.question: Are microexpressions useful for detecting lies?
faq.answer: They indicate concealed emotion, not necessarily deception. Someone may hide fear because they are nervous, not because they are lying. Using microexpressions alone as a lie detection tool is unreliable.
